blocks.text: The Ronan Guillou Grant #4: Human and the Marine World in and around the Sète, Thau Lagoon and Gulf of Lion Region

European and Southern Mediterranean photographers: do you have a project exploring the relationship between people and the marine world? Apply for the 4th edition of the Ronan Guillou Grant and receive €4,000 to develop a photographic project in and around Sète, the étang de Thau and the Golfe du Lion! In October 2026, a call for applications for a photographic creation grant was launched for professional photographers from Europe and the southern shores of the Mediterranean, with the support of Sète Agglopôle Méditerranée, M28-Terres de culture, the Musée ethnographique de l’Étang de Thau, Hahnemühle and the Tomoé laboratory. The Ronan Guillou Grant invites a photographer, for its fourth edition, to develop an engaged photographic project addressing social, cultural, ecological and/or heritage-related issues, exploring the relationship between people and the marine world. The project should explore the challenges of our future in connection with the sea and/or promote a progressive or activist—vision aimed at raising awareness and radically shifting perspectives on these issues. It may address questions relating to ecology, human activity, heritage and transmission, or the relationship between the region and other areas of the Mediterranean basin. This call is open to professional photographers from Europe and the southern shores of the Mediterranean, with no age limit, who wish to develop an engaged photographic project exploring the relationship between people and the Mediterranean Sea in and around Sète, (Occitanie region). The selected photographer will have a two-month period to develop their project. A partial or complete presentation of the work will be organised in September 2027 as part of the FLOW biennial. The residency period will be determined in consultation with the organisers, taking into account the availability and professional and personal commitments of the selected photographer (ongoing commissions, professional or family obligations, etc.). The residency must nevertheless amount to a total of two months, which may be divided into two periods between February and June 2027, according to a schedule jointly agreed upon with the organisers.
